findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: import_url, request_review, get_review, get_job, list_jobs, upload, get_presets · Private data: create_key, import_url, transcribe, request_review, list_jobs, upload, preview, get_presets · Public sink: create_key, caption_video, import_url, upload, manage_preset · Destructive: caption_video, transcribe, batch, remove_silences, request_review, get_glossary, estimate, manage_preset, update_glossary.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: import_url, request_review, get_review, get_job, list_jobs, upload, get_presets · Private data: create_key, import_url, transcribe, request_review, list_jobs, upload, preview, get_presets · Public sink: create_key, caption_video, import_url, upload, manage_preset · Destructive: caption_video, transcribe, batch, remove_silences, request_review, get_glossary, estimate, manage_preset, update_glossary

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "create_key" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
